outcome.technical: Requirement clauses. (1) _task_gate_setup obtains its shape from resolve_shape, one resolver and one order: audit-task.py _task_gate_setup now calls _gate_derive.resolve_shape(phase, build, meta.phaseGate.derived) (about line 2740); the _path_scoped_sibling alias is deleted (about line 2557). _point (about line 2618) fills a spelling via new _gate_derive.point_shape, led by meta.phaseGate.always; _spelled_in words the basis; derive() in _gate_derive.py now calls the same point_shape instead of its inline substitution. (2) Stale comment states what the code does: _gate_derive.py lines 128-134 no longer call the spelling the second source; it says the spelling is the FIRST source tried and that no caller outside picks path_scoped_sibling. (3) A case asserts no caller outside _gate_derive picks a shape source: test__gate_derive.py os1 (the AST detector reports a call, attribute, import, bare name and getattr string), os2 (allow case: resolve_shape, a comment, a docstring are not uses), os3 (walks every .py under SCRIPTS_DIR and HOOKS_DIR except _gate_derive.py, requires the walk to have reached audit-task.py and derive-phase-gate.py, asserts no use). (4) tests.add case: test_audit_task.py tg15 (titled with the tests.add clause verbatim after the id) plus tg15c second-direction case (spelling without {paths} is skipped, sibling read); tg14 updated to assert the alias is gone. (5) verbs-in-full.md wording DID change because behaviour changed: plugins/audit/reference/verbs-in-full.md the three-defaults list and the --failing-from paragraphs now name the recorded spelling first; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md gets one sentence on point_shape and os3. README.md: no wording describes this, not changed. Behaviour change for /audit:task add users: in a plan whose meta.phaseGate.derived.spelling carries {paths}, the task gate is now [meta.phaseGate.always..., spelling filled with the task's quoted tests.add or files paths] and the printed basis reads 'in the spelling meta.phaseGate.derived.spelling records'; before it was the sibling's entry re-pointed. A spelling with no {paths}, or no spelling, behaves exactly as before. The no-sibling-and-no-spelling basis sentence now names both sources. Edge decisions: a gate-only task with no suite files in a spelling-sourced plan with no meta.phaseGate.always gets the phase's wide testGate (source phase-no-paths) because a template has no path-less entry to carry through; the fix-task companion arm (_unit_runner_paths) sees a spelling shape with no path-shaped tokens, so a spelling-sourced plan yields no runner-config companions (before, a sibling supplied them); a spelling-skipped reason that resolve_shape returns is not echoed by add (not done: _task_gate_setup keeps its five-value return that other callers unpack; noted in a comment). Not run: tools/verify.sh and browser gates (forbidden by the orchestrator). Evidence: full `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --quiet` run in the foreground from the task tree, exit 0, 335/335 files ok, 16621 cases; ruff exit 0; vermin exit 0. Mutation proofs in a scratch copy: replacing the resolve_shape call with path_scoped_sibling made tg15 and os3 red and left tg15c green; removing the string-value match in the detector made os2 (allow) and os3 red. The plan gate refused one python heredoc write to audit-task.py ('outside the running task files ... free file already spent on _gate_derive.py'); I did not retry it that way and used the Edit tool, which the gate allowed.
outcome.descriptive: /audit:task add now reads the project's recorded path-scoped spelling first, like derive-phase-gate, through one resolver, and a lint keeps every other script off the sibling source.
